A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, eleven figures, mathematical statements, and Appendix A proofs are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Monte Carlo calculations and forward/backward diffusion simulations, including the non-log-concave examples in Figures 6–11.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original Monte Carlo results and diffusion simulations. These qualify as empirical results despite the paper's primarily theoretical focus.

M1.justification: The forward diffusion maps, score-based backward maps, and Monte Carlo diagnostic procedure are retained. The mathematical corrections and added assumptions do not establish a changed algorithm or implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions study the same six synthetic distributions: point mass, Gaussian, uniform, two point masses, point-mass/Gaussian mixture, and heterogeneous Gaussian mixture. No new evaluation domain or scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated competing algorithms. The newly cited methods in v2 are discussed as related theory, not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains one-dimensional OU simulations with beta = 1, the same distribution parameters and parameter sweeps. Figures 7, 9, and 11 retain T = 100 and eta = 0.01.

E4.justification: The analyses of SNR-dependent localization, nonmonotonic curvature, perturbation complexity M, and forward/backward trajectories are retained. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the simulations. The conditional covariance and survival functions remain theoretical diagnostic quantities, not newly introduced uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 31 plotted panels across Figures 1–11 are identical between the PDFs. The accompanying numerical values and simulation findings, including the SNR bottlenecks and mixture behavior, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 adds lower semicontinuity, minimizer existence, and an admissible stepsize interval; Theorems 2 and 4 add bounded-eigenvalue assumptions. Equation (12) corrects v1's reciprocal noise-scale definition, and Corollary 1 corrects the score derivative to a Hessian. Appendix A corrects coupling indices and an inequality and expands the chaining and tail-integral explanations. The principal bounds and proof strategies remain.

C1.justification: The finite-step optimal-transport claim is qualified: Section 1.2 changes 'any fixed stepsize' to 'a fixed stepsize,' while Proposition 1 replaces all positive stepsizes with an admissible interval under explicit existence conditions. The central curvature, localization, and multi-scale complexity contributions remain.

C2.justification: The newly stated minimizer, stepsize, and bounded-curvature conditions make the guarantees' applicability more explicit. The interpretations of SNR bottlenecks and expansion in the numerical examples, and the stated exclusion of score-estimation error from the paper's focus, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The simulation recipe, distribution parameters, and reported timestep settings are retained. No new implementation, hardware, runtime, sample-count, or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds comparisons with log-concave and weakly log-concave Wasserstein analyses and acknowledges average-curvature arguments in KL analyses, citing Bruno, Gao, Gentiloni-Silveri and Ocello, and Benton. Guo and two Liang works are also added, including a higher-order-denoiser connection in Section 2.2. These extend the existing positioning without replacing it.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the prose, shortens the Section 5 heading, adds an appendix roadmap, updates author and acknowledgement information, and moves references before Appendix A. The main section sequence and overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the presentation with a journal template, revised title and heading styles, larger plot panels and captions, and reflowed mathematical displays. Figures 4 and 5 change from three horizontal panels to two above one, and figures are extensively repositioned. The plotted content itself is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through explicit applicability conditions and corrections to the noise scale, Hessian statement, and appendix expressions. Expanded related-work comparisons and larger figures improve context and readability. These are useful, limited improvements to the same theoretical framework and empirical evidence; the narrower guarantees make their conditions more transparent.
